payload.reason: The evidence provides specific correlations between different variants of ROUGE scores and their effectiveness in evaluating scientific summaries, indicating that different variants yield different correlation values with human judgments.

claims.text: Different variants of ROUGE result in different correlation values with human judgments, indicating that not all ROUGE scores are equally effective.
ROUGE-2 and ROUGE-3 are better correlated with manual judgments in the context of scientific summarization compared to other variants.
There is a large variance of correlations between different ROUGE variants and manual evaluations, affecting the reliability of ROUGE for evaluating scientific summaries.
The proposed metric SERA achieves higher and more consistent correlations with manual assessment scores compared to ROUGE.
